pillar_reactions.evidence: Understood and agreed with no enthusiasm and almost no questions. After the full phase-one description: 'Nope. Straightforward. I assume you guys have an app?' He had already pre-qualified the approach from the free content — 'his workouts seemed the most fun to me, out of the ones that I see' — and had also pre-conceded the coaching point, 'I'm not a savant or thinking that there's nothing to learn.' Nothing on the call moved him; he arrived at that position.

'Make sense? Yep. Cool.' No questions and no pushback, despite this being where his actual problem lives — he had already diagnosed it himself: 'it's not like I eat bad food... I just eat a lot' and 'I do eat as if I was a 20-some-year-old athlete, which I'm not.' A prospect eating at athlete volume on a sedentary lifestyle should have generated far more discussion than one word.

The pillar he named as his entire problem before any pitch — 'mostly just having no accountability. If I'm the one that's holding myself accountable, that's probably not going to happen' — and when it was finally presented he responded 'No, that's pretty clear, pretty straightforward.' The rep never connected the delivery mechanics back to the precise failure mode the prospect had described, that previous programmes 'sort of disconnect from you' after handing over a PDF or an app link. The single most persuasive link available on the call was left unmade.

anchors.raw: I tried Knees Over Toes, actually. I don't know if you know Patrick, whatever his name is. ... I tried his program. It didn't really do much for me.
anchors.note: A cheap, well-known, directly comparable knee-rehab programme that he bought and that failed him. The strongest available proof that self-serve does not work for this prospect, and it was surfaced by the rep's own question and then never used.

anchors.raw: I guess this other, like, Goosh, he has a good program, too, but it's like super heavy lifting kettlebells. It's not interesting for me, and there's others out there that just are not as attractive... it's all these crazy complexes and 700 exercises every time.
anchors.competitor: an unnamed heavy-lifting kettlebell creator, rendered as 'Goosh'
anchors.note: He had already run the comparison across the category and chosen Trevor on sustainability and simplicity, never on price. Useful positioning intelligence: what won was 'if I can do three, four, stay basic, and achieve the same results'.

anchors.raw: I started getting his content in the same way that I get 700 other content creators from within the kettlebell segment
anchors.note: Latent rather than active — he never priced $6,000 against free content and raised no price objection at all. Worth logging because it is the same anchor that blocked other deals in this corpus, sitting dormant in one that closed.

anchors.raw: I have kettlebells here. They're literally 10 feet away from me now. So I'm ready to hit the ground running from that perspective.
anchors.note: No equipment barrier and no start-up delay, which removed the last friction. He framed it himself as a reason to go now.

unmet_demand.want: To know what he is entitled to and what is required of him before paying $6,000
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Asked explicitly and never answered. No terms, cancellation policy, refund conditions, minimum commitment or end-of-term arrangement were stated at any point, and no agreement was seen or signed on the call.

unmet_demand.want: Assurance that loaded kettlebell work will not accelerate bone-on-bone knee degeneration
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Answered with a general customisation promise — 'If there's movements that hurt, okay, well, let's not do those' — from a rep with a month's tenure and no clinical basis. Whether the programme can safely load a joint in this condition is genuinely unestablished either way, and no clinician was involved on either side.

unmet_demand.want: A payment route that works from Europe without a multi-day delay
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The checkout link appears to assume a card or a domestic rail; he had to fall back to a bank transfer taking two to three business days, which delayed access, delayed onboarding and left the sale unsettled at the end of the call.

unmet_demand.want: A programme engaging enough that he returns to it voluntarily — the thing padel does for him and every prior programme failed to do
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He named this as the deciding factor — 'does the program actually make me want to come back? Do I find myself being captivated?' — and it was never addressed. The offer answers convenience and simplicity, not engagement, and his history is that convenience alone has never held him.
